learning_outcomes.text: The student can independently search and understand documentation (schematics, datasheets, programming manuals, ...).
The student can explain the basic concepts and structure of digital hardware.
The student can explain and apply the language, syntax, synthesis, and simulation of VHDL.
The student can develop a solution based on available documentation and problem statement.
The student is able to test/validate a digital design using a testbench and then implement this digital design in an FPGA.

syllabus_topics: VHDL: basic concepts, language, syntax, synthesis, simulation
Design principles and interface design in digital systems
VHDL: basic concepts, language, syntax, synthesis, simulation
Design principles and interface design in digital systems
assessment_rules: The overall grade is composed of 50% for theory and 50% for lab. The theory part is assessed by a written exam. The lab part is assessed by a project, which must meet certain requirements and is developed in consultation with the lecturer. The project includes submission of a video demonstrating its operation and a report. For resits, successful partial results for theory and lab can be carried over within the academic year. If the lab project fails, a new project must be discussed with the lecturer as soon as possible after receiving the first-sit grades.
